assumptions: Exactly the common nonnegative convex cost with at least one finite value, real Hausdorff locally convex E and finite observation subspaces F subset K of the continuous dual.
quantifiers: All records including empty fibers, infinite costs and zero convex coefficients; every finite observation inclusion. No minimizing point is assumed.
domains: Costs have codomain ENNReal, exactly [0,+infinity]. epigraph includes both height>=0 and f(x)<=ofReal(height), so it is the task real-height epigraph even at negative heights. ObservationDual F is the actual algebraic dual with pointwise evaluation topology, which is the ordinary finite-dimensional Hausdorff topology for finite F.
conclusions: All records are nonnegative, convex and finite somewhere. Fiber regrouping proves precisely g_F(y)=inf over restriction(z)=y of g_K(z). Empty fibers give top.
representation: Convexity is proved directly by distributivity of positive scalar multiplication over the actual infima, with zero coefficients split separately; the bridge to epigraph convexity handles all infinite endpoints. Thus it does not require or infer attainment.

assumptions: The common setting plus the task closed real-height epigraph and compact sublevels at every finite nonnegative real c. Negative real sublevels of a nonnegative cost are empty, so this is exactly the relevant compactness requirement.
quantifiers: Every actual finite observation F and every y with g_F(y)<infinity; every finite sublevel c.
domains: The exact real-epigraph definition is proved equivalent to mathlib LowerSemicontinuous for ENNReal costs. The fiber is the closed inverse image of the actual point y under the actual continuous q_F, not a compactification or a chosen abstract model.
conclusions: A finite-cost fiber point determines one compact sublevel. Lower semicontinuity attains a minimum on its closed fiber intersection; this is proved to be the global fiber infimum. The exact equality {g_F<=c}=q_F({f<=c}) then gives compact closed sublevels and hence the closed epigraph.
representation: The compact minimum argument works in arbitrary topological spaces with Hausdorff target; no sequential compactness, metrizability, reflexivity or finite dimension of E is added. Convexity and properness are unnecessary for this stronger compact-fiber lemma.

assumptions: Exactly S2 assumptions, actual compatible y_F for every finite-dimensional continuous-dual subspace and one common finite c>=0 with all record costs<=c.
quantifiers: Every admissible full compatible family and every common bound c; existence and uniqueness of an original x satisfying all observations simultaneously and f(x)<=c.
domains: Each C_F is the intersection of the same original-space compact sublevel {f<=c} with q_F^{-1}(y_F). The family is indexed by all actual FiniteObservation E, including the zero subspace.
conclusions: S2 produces a point in every C_F. The sum of two finite observation spaces gives a common later space, and compatibility gives the reverse-directed inclusions. The compact directed-intersection theorem produces an actual x in all C_F. For uniqueness, the actual complete observation family separates points by Hahn–Banach separation of a point from a closed singleton.
representation: The only extra T2 instance is precisely the task Hausdorff hypothesis. There is no all-record realization assumption or reflexivity assumption. The construction uses the one supplied uniform c, not independent bounds for different F.

assumptions: Only the common setting: nonnegative convex f finite somewhere. No lower semicontinuity or compact sublevel assumption. Competing h range over all EReal functions with closed convex real-height epigraph and h<=f.
quantifiers: All such h, including functions taking negative infinity and positive infinity, all x, and all finite observation inclusions F subset K.
domains: G is literally the supremum over all actual finite F of the closed convex hull of g_F evaluated at q_F x. The continuous affine-minorant construction is proved equal to the closed epigraph construction and to the supremum of genuine real affine minorants, without requiring those minorants themselves to be nonnegative.
conclusions: G is nonnegative, proper, lower semicontinuous and convex, lies below f, and dominates every allowed EReal competitor. Enlarging the observation subspace gives the precise inequality bar(g_F)(restriction z)<=bar(g_K)(z); the reconstruction is a directed supremum. The closed epigraph and every finite or empty vertical section are identified exactly.
representation: The maximum over the full competitor class is proved directly from closed epigraph containment; it never applies a proper-only ENNReal theorem to an EReal competitor. Affine separation treats a zero vertical coefficient by a proved positive perturbation, using nonnegative epigraph heights.

assumptions: Precisely E=R times R and a nonnegative proper convex cost with closed real-height epigraph. No compact-sublevel assumption.
quantifiers: One explicit F, the span of the first-coordinate continuous functional, disproves the universal finite-projection closedness claim. The record formula holds for every actual y in F*.
domains: D is {x>=0,y>=0,xy>=1}, proved equivalent to the task x>0,y>=1/x. f is the actual zero/infinity indicator of D. firstSpace is an actual one-dimensional subspace of E-prime; firstValue and firstLift identify its true dual with R.
conclusions: D is nonempty, closed and convex, hence f meets all hypotheses. The actual g_F(y) is zero iff firstValue(y)>0 and infinity otherwise. Its real-height epigraph is not closed. At the actual zero observation, g_F=infinity and its relaxation is zero.
representation: The proof explicitly transports the coordinate projection to the task finite-observation definition. Nonclosedness is obtained by a continuous pullback and the proved halfline boundary, not merely inferred from an unrelated projection formula.

assumptions: Only the common setting, arbitrary finite F subset K and the actual greatest lower semicontinuous convex minorant operation. The counterexample uses exactly the S5 cost.
quantifiers: Both directions of G=f iff f has closed real-height epigraph; every finite observation inclusion and every record; a concrete instance refuting omission of the outer closure.
domains: The inner infimum is over actual restriction fibers of bar(g_K). Its nonnegativity, convexity and a finite value are proved, so its relaxation is the same valid cost operation. For the counterexample K is the full finite-dimensional continuous dual of R².
conclusions: The precise equality bar(g_F)=bar(inf_restriction bar(g_K)) follows from the two pointwise bounds and maximality. G=f iff f is closed. The full-observation map is an actual continuous linear isomorphism with explicit inverse from the two coordinate evaluations, so bar(g_K)=g_K for the hyperbola cost. At the same F record, the raw inner infimum is infinity while bar(g_F)=0, proving the outer closure cannot be removed.
representation: The original function remains correctly reconstructed despite the nonclosed lower-dimensional projection. No unrestricted commuting of projection and closure is claimed. Both the full and first-coordinate observations are actual subspaces of the prescribed continuous dual.
